claim: On hard328, letting Think-SFT's 16,384-token cap hits finish (its 32,768-cap rows) inside a 4-sample vote turns at least 2 problems the vote had right into wrong ones, because the converted wrong answers now vote against a right minority, while the vote gains less than half of the 23-problem single-sample gain.
why_only_this: Only this mechanism says a cap hit's value to the vote is that it abstains, so turning it into a finished (mostly wrong) answer costs vote-right problems. round-09/grader-m06 and run-08/f2-m02 say how many cap hits turn right when the cap is raised (yield) and how a rescored count differs from a native one. They say nothing about votes, so they predict no flips and a vote gain limited only by the ceiling. run-04/f2-m05 says drifted continuations are wrong, not that they dilute a vote. round-09/grader-m04 compares sets (fresh2026 against hard328), not abstaining against finishing on the same rows. round-09/grader-m01 and run-08/f2-m01 are about seed scatter, round-09/training-m01 is about template answer placement, and round-10/weights-m06 and round-10/problems-m04 are about edit directions and problem strata. None of these predicts that a finished wrong answer takes a right vote away.
computation: 1) Load the Think-SFT + cue cap-32,768 hard328 rows: the per-problem rows in cap32/rows-01 or rows-02, whichever holds the Think-SFT cue arm, or sft_cue-01. Each row needs the problem index, generated tokens, finished or capped, the extracted final answer and right under grader v3. Check that you get 230 right at 32k and 207 when rescored at 16,384 (a row longer than 16,384 tokens counts as a cap hit there). Stop and report if either total does not match. 2) Load thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (4 samples per problem, cap 16,384) and keep samples 1, 2 and 3. Drop sample 0 so that no draw is used twice. 3) For each of the 328 problems, build two 4-vote sets that share samples 1-3. In set A the 4th vote is the cap32 row scored at 16,384: if it is longer than 16,384 tokens it abstains, otherwise it votes its extracted answer. In set B the 4th vote is the same row scored at 32,768: it abstains only if it hit 32,768, otherwise it votes its answer. Rows with no extracted answer abstain in both sets. 4) Vote rule: plurality over the non-abstaining answers. Group answers as equivalent when math-verify 0.9.0 (as in tools/finding_imitation_beats_rl.py) judges them equal, otherwise by exact normalized string. Break ties toward the shortest finished sample. If all 4 abstain, the problem is wrong. A problem is right if the winning group is graded right by v3. 5) Report: G1 = right(row at 32k) - right(row at 16k), about 23. VA = vote-right count in A. VB = vote-right count in B. The vote gain is VB - VA. The converted rows are those capped at 16,384 and finished by 32,768. Count U = problems wrong in A and right in B. Count D = problems right in A and wrong in B. A converted row can only change the vote on its own problem, so every flip is caused by one converted row. For each D problem, record the converted answer, the answers of samples 1-3, and whether the flip came from a plurality or a tie-break. 6) Null A' (abstention): set B, but each converted row that is wrong abstains. This is the ceiling-only prediction of a pure yield mechanism. By construction its D is 0, and VA' - VA gives the ceiling-limited gain. 7) Second-sample null for scatter: among wrong finished answers, compare how often a converted 16k->32k row's answer matches one of samples 1-3 against how often a sample-1 row that finished under 16,384 and was wrong matches samples 2-3. Use Wilson intervals. 8) Repeat steps 1-6 for RL plain, using cap32/rl_plain-01 as the 4th vote and samples 1-3 of day1_3/hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01, as a contrast. RL has 20 cap hits, so expect a smaller G1. Bootstrap VB - VA and (VB - VA)/G1 over problems, 10,000 resamples, seed 0.
refuted_if: For Think-SFT, D <= 1 (converted wrong rows flip at most one vote-right problem), or the vote gain VB - VA is at least half of G1 (the 95 % bootstrap lower bound of (VB - VA)/G1 >= 0.5), or VB >= VA' (letting the wrong converted rows vote costs nothing against the abstention null).
threshold: Holds only if D >= 2, the upper end of the 95 % interval of (VB - VA)/G1 is < 0.5, and VB < VA'. Otherwise it is refuted.
null: A' is the same samples with each converted row that is wrong abstaining instead of voting. This pure yield/ceiling account (grader-m06, f2-m02) predicts zero flips and a gain of VA' - VA. The scatter part is checked against a second Think-SFT sample: 16k-finished wrong rows from sample 1 against samples 2-3 give the base rate at which a wrong vote matches other wrong votes. RL's cap32 row plus 3 RL samples is the cross-model comparison.
